podcast.title: Ninety minutes in a taxi

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: How long is your journey to work or school? Guess: how long did Sam's journey take this morning?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is traffic. And this morning it took me ninety minutes to get to the studio.
[laugh] Ninety minutes! What happened?
Rush hour happened. I took a taxi because I was late, and we sat in a traffic jam for forty minutes.
You should take the metro in the morning. It's faster, and the fare is cheap.
I know, I know. But my taxi driver was very entertaining. He honked at every car, every bus and even a cat.
Drivers here love to honk. It's like a language. One short honk means "hello", a long one means "move!"
And pedestrians? Nobody waits for the green light.
True, people cross everywhere. As a pedestrian in Baku, you need eyes in the back of your head.
In Manchester we wait at the crossing even when the street is empty. It's almost a religion.
And let me guess — the driver took a detour.
How did you know? He said, "I know a short cut." We went through tiny streets, and it took twenty minutes more!
Classic. Do you drive yourself?
Not here. I'm too scared. What about you?
I do, but driving with my dad is terrible. He's the worst back seat driver in the world.
What does he do?
"Slow down! Watch that bus! Why this lane?" And he doesn't even sit in the back seat. He sits next to me!
[laugh] My mum is the same. So how long is your commute?
Only fifteen minutes. I walk to the metro, and I read on the train.
That's the dream. Tomorrow I'll try the metro. I promise.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: how do you get to work or school — and what is your worst traffic story?
Mine is this morning. See you next time!
Bye for now!
